title: Message-level Consumption & Pricing Patterns — Attribution Panel
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design the Console panel that surfaces per-message consumption (tokens + model compute equivalents), allocation attribution to routes/features, and exportable rows for downstream billing systems. This work focuses on UI patterns for compact breakdown rows, flexible grouping filters, CSV/Parquet export schema, and in-context pricing simulation. Goal: give platform engineers and finance teams a single pane of truth for per-request economics while preserving fast scanning in the Console UX.
acceptance_criteria: Panel shows per-message breakdown: prompt tokens, completions tokens, embeddings units where applicable, and inferred compute weight; values align with runtime samples from ENG-3312.
Attribution controls let users group by route, model, customer tag, or custom metadata keys and persist saved views.
Export generates CSV and Parquet with documented column schema and sampling options (full, sampled, aggregated).
Pricing simulation control applies chosen rate-card (hosted/dedicated) and shows projected invoice and delta vs baseline.
Design tokens and component variants provided in Figma with desktop and responsive states.
Accessibility: table rows navigable by keyboard and tooltips readable by screen readers.
decisions: Show per-message rows by default for the last 24h sample; enable toggle to show aggregated daily rows to reduce volume.
Use 'Compute Weight' as a normalized metric (tokens * model-factor) rather than showing raw GPU-seconds in the initial release to avoid telemetry gaps.
Export schema will include both token-level columns and a normalized_cost column to simplify downstream ingestion for finance teams.
